originalTitle: '101-year-old great-grandmother' arrested for selling cannabis in Nigeria
title: A Very Old Grandma and a Big Surprise in Nigeria!
content:
A Very Old Grandma and a Big Surprise!

Hello, amazing friends! Welcome to your news from Africa. Today we have a story that is a little bit surprising, and it comes from a country called Nigeria. It's about a very special person who is super, super old! Imagine someone who has seen so many sunrises and sunsets. Someone who has lived through a hundred and one years! That's right, one hundred and one! That is a very, very long time. This story is about a great-grandmother. Do you know what a great-grandmother is? It’s your grandma’s mother! Wow!

Meet Grandma Esther!

Her name is Grandma Esther Ogunmabo. She is 101 years old. Can you imagine being that old? She must have so many stories to tell about how the world has changed. Grandma Esther lives in a beautiful country in West Africa called Nigeria. Nigeria is a country full of many friendly people, wonderful music, and delicious food! It's one of the biggest countries in Africa. Did you know? A 101-year-old person has lived for more than 36,000 days! That's a lot of birthdays and a lot of life!

What Happened?

Now, here comes the surprising part of the story. The police in Nigeria came to Grandma Esther. They think she was selling something that is against the rules. They call it a special plant. The police said that Grandma Esther was selling small packets of this plant. People call this plant “cannabis” or sometimes “skunk” – but it’s really just a special kind of plant that is not allowed to be sold. When the police take someone because they think they broke a rule, we say they are ‘arrested’. So, Grandma Esther was arrested because the police think she was selling these small packets of the not-allowed plant. Did you know? Police officers wear uniforms and help keep everyone safe by making sure people follow the rules. They are like friendly helpers in our towns and cities!

Why Are There Rules About This Plant?

Why are some plants not allowed to be sold? Well, just like some berries in the forest are not good to eat, some plants are not good for people. They can make people feel very sick or confused. Our grown-ups and our governments make rules to keep everyone safe and healthy. Selling or using this special plant is against the rules in many places, including Nigeria, because it can be bad for people's bodies and minds. These rules are very important. They help make sure our communities are safe places for children and grown-ups to live and play. It’s like when your parents say, “Don’t touch the hot stove!” It’s for your safety! Did you know? Nigeria is famous for its lively music and movies, which many people around Africa and the world enjoy!

The Police Are Here to Help!

When the police heard that someone might be selling this not-allowed plant, they had to go and check. Their job is to protect everyone and make sure the rules are followed. So, even though Grandma Esther is very, very old, the police still had to do their job. They need to find out exactly what happened and why this plant was being sold. It’s a serious job, but it’s important for keeping our neighbourhoods safe for all of us, from the youngest babies to the oldest grandmas.

What Happens Next?

When someone is arrested, it doesn't mean they are definitely guilty. It means the police will ask more questions and look for more clues. They need to find out the truth. Then, sometimes, people go to a special place called a court. A judge, who is like a super-smart grown-up who knows all the rules, listens to everyone. They help decide what is true and what should happen next. This process takes time, and everyone gets a chance to tell their side of the story. We hope that Grandma Esther will be treated kindly while everyone finds out what really happened. Did you know? In many African cultures, elders like grandmothers and grandfathers are very respected for their wisdom and experience. They are like walking history books!

Important Lessons for All of Us!

This story might sound a bit sad, but it teaches us some important things. First, rules are for everyone. It doesn't matter if you are 7 years old or 101 years old, we all need to follow the rules to keep our communities happy and safe. Second, it's always good to make kind and smart choices. Think about what you do and if it's a good choice for you and for others. And third, we should always respect our elders. Grandmas and great-grandmas have a lot of wisdom to share. We should listen to them and help them if they need it.

A Special Note About Nigeria

Nigeria is a country with a very big heart! People there love to sing, dance, and tell amazing stories. It’s a place where families are very important, and communities often help each other. This story is just one small thing that happened, but it doesn't change how wonderful Nigeria and its people are.

Let's Remember to Be Kind

So, while we hear about this surprising story, let's remember to be kind to everyone. Let’s think about how important rules are, and always try to make good choices. And let's send kind thoughts to Grandma Esther and all the people in Nigeria. We hope that everything will be sorted out with fairness and care. See you next time for more news from Africa!
summary: A 101-year-old great-grandmother named Esther Ogunmabo in Nigeria was taken by the police because they think she sold small packets of a plant that is against the rules.
whyMatters: This story helps us remember that rules are important for everyone, no matter how old they are, and we should always try to make good choices to keep our communities safe.

originalTitle: Syrian president thanks nation for getting off US state terror list
title: Good News! Syria is Not on the 'Special List' Anymore!
content:
Hello, Friends! Big News from Far Away!

Hello, amazing kids! Your friendly news reporter for Africa is here with some exciting news from a country far, far away. It's about a place called Syria. Imagine a country that had some big problems, like when friends argue, but now things are getting much better! We have a special announcement about Syria and its leader, President Ahmed al-Sharaa. He is very, very happy. He has a big smile and wants to say a huge thank you to everyone in his country. This is because something good happened!

Who is President Ahmed al-Sharaa?

So, who is a president? Imagine your school's head teacher. The head teacher helps everyone in the school, makes sure rules are fair, and tries to keep everyone happy and safe. Well, a president is like that, but for a whole country! President Ahmed al-Sharaa is the leader of Syria. His job is to look after all the people who live in Syria. He helps them, he listens to them, and he tries to make his country a wonderful place for everyone, especially for children like you!

Where is Syria?

Syria is a country very far from us here in Africa. If you look at a big map of the world, you would find it in a place called the Middle East. It's on a different continent, but we are all still neighbors on our big planet Earth! Syria has lots of beautiful places, just like our countries in Africa. It has cities with busy streets, small villages, and even ancient buildings that are very, very old. Many people, families, and children live there. Did you know? Countries are like big families! Everyone tries to work together to make things good.

What Was the 'Special List'?

Now, for the really important part of our news story. Syria was on a 'special list' for a long, long time. Imagine you have a 'naughty list' at school. If someone is on that list, it means they might have broken some rules or caused problems. This 'special list' was made by a very big country called America, also known as the USA. When a country was on this list, it meant that America and other countries thought that the country had some big, big troubles. They thought maybe there was fighting or that things were not very safe. Being on this list made things very hard for Syria. Other countries found it difficult to send help, like food or medicine. It was also hard for people to visit Syria or for Syria to buy things from other countries. It was almost like being put in 'time out' for a whole country.

Why is Getting Off the List So Good?

But guess what? Syria is now OFF this 'special list'! Hooray! This is wonderful news! It means that things are changing in Syria for the better. It means that the big problems are starting to go away, and peace is growing. When a country gets off such a list, it's like saying, "Okay, you've learned your lesson, and you're ready to play nicely again." It means that Syria can now be better friends with other countries all around the world. Think about it! If you were on a naughty list and then got off it, wouldn't you feel happy? It means trust is coming back. It means people believe in Syria again. This is a very big step towards a brighter future for everyone there. Did you know? When countries are friends, they can share ideas, help each other, and even learn new games!

President Sharaa Says 'Thank You' to Everyone!

President Ahmed al-Sharaa is so happy about this good news. He stood up and said a big, big thank you to all the people in Syria. He thanked the moms, the dads, the grandmas, the grandpas, and even the children! He thanked them because everyone in Syria helped make this happen. They worked hard to make their country better and safer. It's like when your whole class works together to clean the classroom, and the teacher says, "Good job, everyone!" The president knows that it takes everyone working together to solve big problems. He is proud of his country and wants them to know it. This thank you shows that he cares a lot about his people.

What Does This Mean for Syria's Children?

This is especially good news for the children of Syria. When a country is off a 'special list' and things get better, it often means more peace. More peace means kids can play outside more safely. It means more children can go to school every day without worry. It means families can live in their homes without being scared. It means there can be more toys, more food, and more doctors to help when someone is sick. Did you know? Every child in the world wants to play, learn, and feel safe! This news helps Syria's children get closer to that dream.

Friendship for the Future!

So, President Sharaa's thank you is not just for today. It's a thank you for all the hard work that will lead to a better future for Syria. It means that Syria can look forward to new friendships with countries far and wide, including our own countries here in Africa. When one country finds more peace and happiness, it helps the whole world feel a little bit better. We are all connected on this planet. So let's cheer for Syria and hope for even more good news to come! This is your friendly news reporter for Africa, signing off! Keep being curious and kind, kids!
summary: Syria's President Ahmed al-Sharaa is very happy and thanked his country because Syria is no longer on a special 'terror list' made by America, meaning things are getting better and safer for everyone there.
whyMatters: This is important because it means Syria is becoming a more peaceful place, so other countries can be friends with them, send help, and children can live and learn more safely.

title: A Kind Promise from Far Away Lands!
content:
Jambo, amazing children of Africa! Your friendly news reporter is here, ready to share a super important story with you today. It's about helping friends, being brave, and why standing together makes us all stronger! Imagine you have a friend who needs help, maybe with a tricky puzzle or sharing their toys. What do you do? You help them, right? That's what this story is all about!

Meet Our Friend, Mr. Leo, from Rainbow Land!

Far, far away, across big oceans and many lands, there's a beautiful country called Rainbow Land. It's like a big village, and in charge of everything there is a very kind man named Mr. Leo. He's like the head teacher of the whole country, making sure everyone is safe and happy. He has a very important job, and he tries his best to be a good friend to other countries all around the world. Did you know? The United Kingdom, or UK for short, is the real name of Rainbow Land! It's an island country in Europe, known for its kings, queens, and sometimes, a lot of rain! Mr. Leo heard that one of his friends, a country called Sunflower Valley, was having a difficult time. Sunflower Valley is a lovely place, but it needs a little extra help and friendship right now. So, Mr. Leo, with his big heart, made a promise. He promised that Rainbow Land would keep helping Sunflower Valley, no matter what!

Helping Our Friends in Sunflower Valley

Sunflower Valley is a country far away, like a neighbour's big farm, filled with sunshine and fields. But sometimes, even good places can face challenges. Sunflower Valley is going through a tough time, and they need help from their friends. Helping means giving them good things they need, like food or blankets, or even special tools. It also means being a good friend and saying, "We are here for you!" Rainbow Land has been sending special things to Sunflower Valley. These things are meant to help Sunflower Valley stay strong and safe. Think of it like sharing your best crayons with a friend who has run out, or giving them a big hug when they're sad. It shows you care!

Little Flying Helpers: What are Drones?

Now, here's where it gets interesting! Sunflower Valley has been using some cool gadgets from Rainbow Land. These gadgets are called "drones." What are drones? Imagine a super-cool remote-control airplane or a tiny flying robot! They can fly high in the sky and do amazing things. Sometimes they take pictures, sometimes they can carry small packages, and sometimes they help people see things from far away without having to go there themselves. Did you know? In some parts of Africa, drones are used to deliver important medicine to faraway villages! They fly medicines over mountains and rivers much faster than a car can drive, helping people get better quickly. Sunflower Valley was using these little flying helpers from Rainbow Land. These drones are like extra eyes in the sky, helping them to keep an eye on things and stay safe during their difficult time. It's like having a little bird flying around, telling you what's happening from up high!

The Growly Voice from Snowflake Mountains

But not everyone was happy about this. Another country, which we'll call Snowflake Mountains, heard about Sunflower Valley using the drones from Rainbow Land. Snowflake Mountains is a very big country, and sometimes, it can be a little grumpy, just like when someone doesn't want to share their toys. Snowflake Mountains made some "growly noises" and said some "unfriendly warnings." They said that if Rainbow Land kept helping Sunflower Valley, there might be "consequences." This means they were saying, "Watch out! If you keep helping, something not nice might happen!" Did you know? The capital city of Russia, which is our 'Snowflake Mountains', is called Moscow. Sometimes, when news talks about Moscow, they mean the whole country of Russia and its leaders. These growly noises were meant to make Mr. Leo and Rainbow Land scared, so they would stop helping Sunflower Valley. But Mr. Leo is very brave!

Mr. Leo's Brave Promise

Mr. Leo heard the growly noises from Snowflake Mountains, but he didn't get scared. Instead, he stood up tall and said, "No! We will not stop helping our friends!" He said that even with these "outrageous threats" – which means very, very strong and not-nice warnings – Rainbow Land will continue to support Sunflower Valley. He thinks it's super important to be a loyal friend. He believes that helping a friend in need is the right thing to do, no matter what. It's like when you promise to help your friend build a sandcastle, and even if another kid comes by and says grumpy things, you still finish the castle together! That's what being a true friend means.

Why It's Good to Help Friends

This story teaches us a very important lesson: friendship and kindness are super powerful! When you help a friend, you make them feel happy and safe. You show them that they are not alone. And when countries help other countries, they build a better, happier world for everyone. Did you know? Many countries around the world work together like a big family to help each other when there are problems, like floods, earthquakes, or difficulties like the one in Sunflower Valley. This is called international cooperation! Mr. Leo's promise is like a big, warm hug from Rainbow Land to Sunflower Valley, saying "We are with you!" It shows that bravery isn't just about fighting; it's also about standing up for what's right and being a good friend, even when others try to make you stop. So, my wonderful friends, remember Mr. Leo's story. Remember to always be kind, always be helpful, and always be a good friend, just like Rainbow Land is being to Sunflower Valley. Your reporter from Africa, signing off! Keep shining brightly!
